question: Does the Agusan Marsh source that mentions Barangay San Marcos and Lake Mihaba provide evidence about San Marcos Lake in Capas, Tarlac?

agusanMarsh.administrativeAreaAsReported: Bunawan, Agusan del Sur, Region XIII
agusanMarsh.reportedContent: A community focus-group table provides a set of local/common fish names for Barangay San Marcos (Lake Mihaba).
agusanMarsh.supports: Disambiguation: the San Marcos wording in this Agusan Marsh report is a barangay/locality paired with Lake Mihaba in Bunawan, Agusan del Sur, not San Marcos Lake in Capas, Tarlac.
doesNotSupport: a relationship between Lake Mihaba and the Capas lake
transfer of the Agusan local fish list to Tarlac

agusanFishStudyCrossReference.interpretation: The existing review concerns the separate Agusan Marsh floodplain lake Mihaba and other named Agusan lakes. It is not evidence for the Capas waterbody; its historical lake-presence matrix must remain scoped to its own study sites.

synthesis.identity: The shared words San Marcos are insufficient to merge places. The Tarlac source names a lake in Capas; the Agusan report names a barangay associated with Lake Mihaba in Bunawan, Agusan del Sur.
synthesis.fishEvidence: Capas has a reported stocking event only in the reviewed source set. The Agusan community table and Agusan fish study cannot be transferred to Capas or treated as a Capas fish roster.
synthesis.publicUse: No species, occurrence, diet, geometry, safety, or app row is admitted. Both the Capas baseline and Central Luzon remain incomplete.

nextActions: Keep the Agusan Marsh San Marcos/Lake Mihaba material out of the Capas evidence lane.
Seek a dated, taxon-resolved fish survey or voucher-backed record explicitly tied to San Marcos Lake, Capas, Tarlac.
Keep San Marcos Lake, Central Luzon, and Luzon marked incomplete.

sources.supports: Historical Capas stocking event and the Tarlac administrative locality; no lake fish inventory.
Official DENR/ADB report identifies Lake Mihaba in Bunawan and prints a separate focus-group row for Barangay San Marcos (Lake Mihaba); it does not concern Capas, Tarlac.
Previously reviewed historical fish-composition paper for named Agusan Marsh lakes including Mihaba, kept out of the Tarlac scope.
